final_message:
**Status: verified** (local-full, full precision). The model compares two token counts, and five of its 15 components do the work.

**Algorithm**
```
n_fo = count of "fo" (id 2) in the 5 input tokens
n_ni = count of "ni" (id 4)
n_fo > n_ni -> J (7);  n_fo < n_ni -> V (8);  tie -> Y (9)
```
The tokens le, pe and ti, and the positions of the tokens, play no part.

**Circuit: `mlp0`, `1.1`, `1.2`, `mlp1`, `mlp2`**
- **Head 1.1 counts fo and head 1.2 counts ni.** On prompts without ni, ablating 1.1 drops the metric to 0.0 while 1.2 leaves it at 1.0; on prompts without fo it is exactly the reverse (E0009, E0010).
- **All three MLPs are individually necessary.** Mean-ablating any one of them leaves about 0 of the clean metric (E0011).
- **The other 10 heads are inert.** All of layer 0, 1.0, 1.3 and all of layer 2 can be mean-ablated together with the metric staying at 1.0 (E0005).

**Verification (V0001, held-out seed 777, n=200)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `predict()` vs model | 200/200 agreement (null p95 0.39) |
| Circuit ablated | metric -0.02, accuracy 0.29 (chance) |
| Everything else ablated | metric 1.0, accuracy 1.0 |
| Null controls | all three passed |

**Predictions:** 6 pre-registered, 6 confirmed, 0 refuted.

**Budget:** 12 of 25 experiments used (6 pre-registered, 5 exploratory, plus the dataset inspection), and one verification.

**What is not established**
- The membership of the circuit is causal, but the wiring inside it is not: the edges mlp0 → heads and mlp1 → mlp2 are inferred from layer order and necessity, not path-patched.
- What mlp0 writes, and why the comparison needs two MLP layers, are open questions.
- Head 1.1 splitting attention equally over BOS and the fo positions rests on one exploratory prompt (E0008); head 1.2's pattern was not inspected directly.
- The function was checked on 200 held-out random inputs, not all 3125 possible ones.

The first `write_report` call failed with a KeyError when V0001 was listed under key plots; I removed it from the plots and it is still cited as evidence in the claims.
